content_preview.title: PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 Moves General Availability to November 19, With a Second Release Candidate Planned for November 12
content_preview.summary: PostgreSQL 19 RC 1, posted October 15, sets general availability for November 19, 2026, and plans RC 2 for November 12 alongside the next scheduled update release.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group posted the first release candidate of PostgreSQL 19 on October 15, 2026, and set a general availability date of November 19, 2026, [according to the RC 1 announcement](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-19-rc-1-released-3409/). The announcement also says a second release candidate, RC 2, will be published on November 12, the same day as the next scheduled update release for supported PostgreSQL versions.

editor_notes.content_quality: Concise Briefing (556 words, within the 300-800 range) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Leads with the verifiable schedule change and keeps the bug-fix list tightly scoped to the announcement.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots (source-0.html.gz = RC 1 announcement, posted 2026-10-15; source-1.html.gz = Beta 4 announcement, posted 2026-09-24); both are complete full-text captures (status 200, suspicious_patterns null), so the snapshots were sane. As an extra check, both live URLs were re-fetched with WebFetch and the relevant passages matched the snapshots exactly. source-0 confirms: RC 1 posted 2026-10-15; GA planned November 19, 2026; RC 2 planned November 12, 2026; RC 2 'on the same day as the update release'; next scheduled update release on November 12, 2026; verbatim quotes 'will include a large number of fixes', 'decided to include these fixes in PostgreSQL 19 before its general availability', 'Unless an issue is discovered that requires a delay or an additional release candidate' (article's '[u]nless' bracketed capitalisation is a legitimate alteration), and 'will be mostly identical to the initial release of PostgreSQL 19, though some more fixes may be applied prior to the general availability of PostgreSQL 19.' All seven bug-fix bullets match the 'Changes Since 19 Beta 4' list item for item (REPACK (CONCURRENTLY), pg_plan_advice, NULL-ability planner optimizations, logical replication enablement with wal_level=replica, postgres_fdw statistics import owner, parallel autovacuum, COPY (query) TO FORMAT json column names/aliases). The upgrade statement (pg_upgrade or pg_dump / pg_restore) and the pointer to the open items page match. source-1 confirms verbatim 'should occur in early October' and 'the PostgreSQL 19 GA may also occur in October' (article quotes 'PostgreSQL 19 GA may also occur in October,' - exact substring), and 'potentially be included in a later major release after more time working through the community development and review process' (verbatim; source has the typo 'can be potentially be' outside the quoted span). The Beta 4 list contains six revert bullets including 'Revert SQL/PGQ (property graph query) support', consistent with the 'six features' framing. 'Three weeks earlier' = Sep 24 to Oct 15, correct.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every date, quote and attribution traces to the cited announcements. The characterisation of Beta 4 ('early October' RC, GA 'may also occur in October') is accurate and appropriately hedged. The article correctly notes the RC 1 announcement does not state a cause for the later GA date and only attributes the extra RC 2 to the volume of fixes in the November 12 update release; this is not overstated. The 'previously reported' claim is backed by our own article 2026-09/25-postgresql-19-beta-4-reverts-six-features-..., which exists on main with that exact slug, and the link uses the correct /article/<YYYY-MM>/<slug> form so it resolves. Orphan-link diff: body URLs are exactly the two URLs in article.sources (no bidirectional gap); the only other link is the internal one.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing or AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Follow-up with new information (schedule change, RC 1 contents) to the Beta 4 article of Sep 25; not a duplicate. No prior RC 1 coverage in the archive.
